Definition: to lay hold of; especially to pick up fire
BiblicalUsage: To take up is the word for snatching up coals, and it carries fire in every use. Isaiah pictures a broken vessel with no sherd left to take fire from the hearth, Proverbs asks whether a man can take fire in his bosom unburned, and the same coals are heaped on an enemy's head by kindness.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe fire is the right picture for this word, because what we take up either burns us or blesses us. Kindness that heaps coals on an enemy's head is fire put to its proper use.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
